land.text: the centre and north of Spain that the French held in 1808: Cliopatria's Kingdom of Spain shape of 1808 minus its 1809 shape

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the French-held parts of Spain 1809-1813 inside its First French Empire shapes; the Kingdom of Spain dossier books them to first-french-empire.

land.text: the Spain restored to Ferdinand VII: Vitoria (21 June 1813), Valencia evacuated after it, and the Treaty of Valencay (8 December 1813)

capitals.name: Madrid
capitals.note: Joseph entered Madrid on 20 July 1808, evacuated it on 1 August, was restored on 1 December 1808; left on 11 August 1812 and again on 17 March 1813.

rulers.name: Joseph Bonaparte (José I)
rulers.note: Made king on 15 June 1808 (Joseph page; the Peninsular War page: crowned 25 July); permanently left Spain in June 1813.

correction.text: the centre and north that the French held: Madrid (restored on 1 December 1808), the French-occupied north (Navarre, Catalonia from February 1808) and Old Castile behind the Ebro

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row; its Kingdom of Spain shape of 1809-1810 (233.6 thousand km2) is the unoccupied part and its First French Empire shape of 1809-1810 (1.06 M km2) carries the French-held Spain. No infobox area (the Joseph page gives none). The 1808 coverage of June-November is the same centre-and-north reading; the pages date Madrid (20 July-1 August, then 1 December).

correction.text: the centre and north without the four military governments (Biscay, Navarre, Aragon, Catalonia, 'dependent on Paris from 1810'), plus Andalusia except Cádiz ('The French invaded Andalusia on 19 January 1810')

keyframe_review.note: Cádiz stayed free under siege (1810-1812). Cliopatria's own free-zone shape shrinks to 132.2 thousand km2 in 1811.

correction.text: as 1810-1811 plus Valencia, taken by Suchet on 9 January 1812; from 11-14 August 1812 Madrid, Castile, León and Andalusia are lost

keyframe_review.note: The year changes at 11 August (Madrid abandoned) and by August the French end the siege of Cádiz; the ledger carries the losses.

correction.text: the north and east of the peninsula, Valencia and the north, until Vitoria on 21 June 1813, without the military governments (Biscay, Navarre, Aragon, Catalonia); Madrid is Joseph's until 17 March 1813

keyframe_review.note: After Salamanca (22 July 1812) 'the French held only scattered garrisons across much of their former territory' (Peninsular War page). fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): Valencia added. The 1814 shape minus the 1812 shape leaves it out (Cliopatria's 1812 shape holds Valencia), although the text always said 'Valencia, the north': Suchet took it on 9 January 1812 and held it 'until the French defeat at Vitoria on 21 June 1813, after which he was forced to evacuate Valencia' (Suchet page); the Peninsular War page has Joseph and Jourdan retreat to Valencia.

region.text: the centre and north held by the French

ledger.note: 15 June 1808: Joseph Bonaparte is made King of Spain. 'The Council of Castile assembled in Bayonne and ratified the transfer of the Crown'; the Bayonne Statute follows on 7 July 1808; Joseph entered Madrid on 20 July and was crowned on 25 July (Peninsular War page). The pages name Madrid and the French-occupied provinces, not a boundary.
June 1808: Spain under Joseph is a Napoleonic client state (page: 'a Napoleonic client state that existed from 1808 to 1813').
1 August 1808: after Bailén 'Joseph evacuated the capital for Old Castile' and the French army sheltered behind the Ebro (the Joseph page: he left Madrid in July after Bailén).

region.text: the centre and north, Madrid restored

ledger.note: 1 December 1808: 'Madrid surrendered on 1 December and Joseph Bonaparte was restored to his throne' (the Joseph page: 2 December) after Napoleon's campaign.
1810: 'Biscay, Navarre, and Aragon were military governments dependent on Paris from 1810', and Catalonia too; Catalonia is 'territory annexed to the French Empire' from 1812 (infobox).
19 January 1810: 'The French invaded Andalusia on 19 January 1810' and took most of the south except Cádiz; the Junta dissolved itself on 29 January.
9 January 1812: Suchet takes Valencia: 'on 9 January 1812 after a brief siege'. The page names the city; the province is the reading.

region.text: Madrid, Castile, Leon and all of Andalusia: the free shape of 1812 without Valencia (which Suchet holds) plus the whole of Andalusia

ledger.note: August 1812: Joseph's state loses the centre and Andalusia. 'King Joseph Bonaparte abandoned Madrid on 11 August' after Salamanca (22 July); Madrid 'surrendered on 14 August'; 'The French were forced to abandon Andalusia for fear of being cut off by the allied armies' (the siege of Cadiz ended with Soult's retreat set for 24 August). The extent is Cliopatria's free shape of 1812 plus all of Andalusia; Valencia is left out because Suchet holds it ('Because Suchet had a secure base at Valencia, Joseph and Marshal Jourdan retreated there') and stays Joseph's until Vitoria. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): this was the 1812 shape minus the 1811 shape, which left Granada, Jaen, Almeria and the other cells of Cliopatria's 1811 'free zone' in Joseph's hands until the 1813 keyframe snap released them to nobody (about 200 cells, 105 of them Andalusian).

region.text: Madrid, Joseph back in the capital

ledger.note: Late 1812: Joseph is again in Madrid; the page is silent on the return and the date is inferred from his leaving Madrid again on 17 March 1813. A gap to fill.
17 March 1813: Joseph leaves Madrid for the last time ('on 17 March el rey intruso').

region.text: the north and east: Valencia and the rest of what Joseph's state still holds

ledger.note: 21 June 1813: Vitoria. 'Joseph's army was defeated' at the Battle of Vitoria on 21 June and he 'permanently left Spain in June' (Joseph page). The French kept Catalonia (annexed from 1812), which was never Joseph's. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): Valencia added: Suchet held it 'until the French defeat at Vitoria on 21 June 1813, after which he was forced to evacuate Valencia' (Suchet page; no day given), so it goes with the rest in June 1813. Everything the state still holds now goes to kingdom-of-spain in June 1813; p1810-p1819 events/4 is no longer needed.
June 1813: Joseph 'permanently left Spain in June'; the client kingdom has no land left. The Treaty of Valençay of 8 December 1813 'aimed to restore' Ferdinand VII (Treaty page).

region.text: the remains of Joseph's Spain (the north and east with Valencia)

ledger.note: June 1813: Joseph permanently leaves Spain; the Treaty of Valençay of 8 December 1813 restores Ferdinand VII and the Cortes of Cádiz repudiated it (Treaty page). The page's infobox ends the state in 1813.

wars.name: Peninsular War
wars.outcome: The French invaded in February 1808, Joseph was restored on 1 December 1808, Andalusia fell in January 1810, Valencia in January 1812; Salamanca (22 July 1812) and Vitoria (21 June 1813) ended Joseph's rule.
wars.note: The war itself outlasted Joseph's rule (the Kingdom of Spain dossier has it end in April 1814; not on the pages opened here).

certainty.note: Occupation fronts moved with every campaign and the pages name cities and provinces only; each extent is a reading anchored on Cliopatria's free-zone shapes of the Kingdom of Spain.

sources.title: Spain under Joseph Bonaparte
sources.note: Infobox 1808-1813, king 15 June 1808, Bayonne Statute 7 July 1808, flight and return, military governments from 1810, Catalonia annexed 1812, left Madrid March 1813, Valençay December 1813; no area.

sources.title: Peninsular War
sources.note: Dated course 1808-1813: Madrid 20 July/25 July/1 August 1808, 1 December 1808, Andalusia 19 January 1810, Valencia 9 January 1812, Salamanca, 11 and 14 August 1812, 17 March 1813, Vitoria 21 June 1813.

sources.title: Treaty of Valençay
sources.note: Signed 8 December 1813 (not 11 December); restores Ferdinand VII; repudiated by the Cortes of Cádiz.

sources.title: Louis-Gabriel Suchet
sources.note: fx-54 (E04): Suchet 'received the capitulation of Valencia on 9 January 1812' and held it 'until the French defeat at Vitoria on 21 June 1813, after which he was forced to evacuate Valencia' (no day given for the evacuation).

notes: Written for eu-12-x (suggested by eu-12-m as bonapartist-spain; 1808-1813 is after the group's era to 1789 but its Spain dossier already covers the years); three pages. Double-booking to reconcile: Cliopatria draws the French-held Spain of 1809-1813 inside its First French Empire shapes, and the kingdom-of-spain dossier books the 1808, 1810, 1812 and 1813 losses and gains with first-french-empire as counterpart; this dossier books the same land to Joseph's client kingdom with kingdom-of-spain as counterpart and first-french-empire as the suzerain (vassal tint). The reconciler should replace first-french-empire with bonapartist-spain in the Spanish dossier's four events (land inside the military governments stays French). Conflicts between pages: Joseph made king 15 June 1808 (Joseph page) or crowned 25 July (Peninsular War page); Madrid restored 1 December (Peninsular War) or 2 December (Joseph); his flight in July after Bailén (Joseph) or 1 August (Peninsular War). Not settled: the 1809 fronts (Zaragoza, Extremadura, Galicia are on neither page), where Joseph's authority ended inside the Old Castile and Leon military zones, the date of Joseph's return to Madrid in 1812 (confidence-1 event), and the provinces inside the military governments. Cádiz stayed free. Gazetteer: Andalusia, Aragon, Catalonia, Navarre are regions; Cádiz, Valencia, Madrid, Bizkaia admin1 exist. fx-54 (3 Nov 2026): the August 1812 loss (ledger/7) now takes all of Andalusia and the whole 1812 free shape except Valencia, and the 1813 keyframe, ledger/10 and the dissolve hold Valencia, so that nothing Joseph's state held is left to nobody between August 1812 and June 1813.
